subject: chemistry
title: Limiting reactants
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) In a reaction with two reactants, one is often in excess. The reactant that is completely used up is the limiting reactant. It limits the amount of product, so the amount of product is worked out from the limiting reactant.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Reactants are not always mixed in exactly the right amounts. This section covers what happens when one runs out first.

items.meaning: The reactant that is completely used up. It limits the amount of products.
The reactant that is left over when the reaction stops.

items: An excess of one reactant is often used to make sure all of the other reactant reacts.
When the limiting reactant is used up, the reaction stops.
Adding more of the excess reactant does not make more product.
Adding more of the limiting reactant makes more product.

blocks.label: Magnesium and hydrochloric acid
where: 1 mol of Mg needs 2 mol of HCl.
0.5 mol of Mg and 0.5 mol of HCl: only 0.25 mol of Mg can react, so Mg is in excess.

items: The limiting reactant is used up first.
The limiting reactant decides how much product forms.
The excess reactant is left over.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Compare the moles you have with the moles the equation needs. The ratio from the equation is essential.

items.text: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → 2Fe + Al₂O₃. The mixture is 1.00 kg of Al and 3.00 kg of Fe₂O₃. Ar: Al = 27, Fe = 56, O = 16.
18.75 mol of Fe₂O₃ needs 2 × 18.75 = 37.5 mol of Al.
There is only 37.0 mol of Al, which is less than 37.5 mol. Aluminium is the limiting reactant.

items: Do not compare the moles directly. 37.0 is not the same as 18.75, but the equation needs twice as many moles of Al.
Do not decide by the masses alone. Convert to moles first.
Use the moles of the **limiting** reactant and the ratio to find the moles of product.
For 108 g of Al (4 mol) with 1.21 kg of CuCl₂ in 2Al + 3CuCl₂ → 3Cu + 2AlCl₃: 4 mol of Al makes 6 mol of Cu, but 8.996 mol of CuCl₂ could make 8.996 mol.
Al is limiting, so the mass of Cu = 6 × 63.5 = 381 g.

diagram.alt: Practise finding the moles of hydrogen made when one reactant limits the reaction.
working: Moles of Mg = {m} ÷ 24. Mg : H₂ = 1 : 1, so Mg could make {m} ÷ 24 mol of H₂
HCl : H₂ = 2 : 1, so 0.40 mol of HCl could make 0.40 ÷ 2 = 0.20 mol of H₂
The limiting reactant gives the smaller amount: **{answer} mol**
diagram.question: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. **{m} g** of magnesium (Ar = 24) reacts with 0.40 mol of hydrochloric acid. Calculate the number of moles of hydrogen made.

items: Moles of each reactant, then use the equation ratio.
The reactant that runs out first is limiting.
Use the limiting reactant to find the amount of product.

checks.a: The reactant that is completely used up, so it limits the amount of product formed.

checks.q: 0.5 mol of hydrochloric acid is mixed with 0.5 mol of magnesium: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Which is in excess?
checks.a: Magnesium. 0.5 mol of HCl reacts with only 0.25 mol of Mg, so Mg is in excess.

checks.q: Why is it wrong to say 18.75 mol of Fe₂O₃ is limiting because 18.75 is less than 37.0 mol of Al in 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → 2Fe + Al₂O₃?
checks.a: The equation needs 2 mol of Al for each 1 mol of Fe₂O₃. 18.75 mol of Fe₂O₃ needs 37.5 mol of Al, so Al is limiting.

worked_example.question:
A mixture contains 1.00 kg of aluminium and 3.00 kg of iron oxide.

The equation for the reaction is:

2Al + Fe₂O₃ → 2Fe + Al₂O₃

Relative atomic masses (Ar): O = 16, Al = 27, Fe = 56

Show that aluminium is the limiting reactant.
answer_points: Aluminium is limiting because 37.0 mol is less than the 2 × 18.75 = 37.5 mol needed (1)
worked_example.tip: Saying that the iron oxide is in excess, because 18.75 mol is more than the 18.5 mol needed, also scores the last mark.

worked_example.question:
The balanced equation for this reaction is

Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂

In a further experiment, 0.5 mol of hydrochloric acid, HCl, were mixed with 0.5 mol of magnesium, Mg.

Use the equation to show that, in this experiment, the magnesium is in excess.
answer_points: The equation shows two HCl reacting with one Mg, so 0.5 mol of HCl reacts with 0.25 mol of Mg. There is 0.5 mol of Mg, so Mg is in excess.
worked_example.tip: Any one of: ratio 2 : 1, 1 mol HCl reacts with 0.5 mol Mg, or 0.5 mol HCl reacts with 0.25 mol Mg.

worked_example.question:
The student reacts the magnesium carbonate they have made with hydrochloric acid.

The student uses 0.2 mol of hydrochloric acid in the reaction. The hydrochloric acid is the limiting reagent.

At the end of the reaction, 0.82 g of magnesium carbonate is left unreacted.

Calculate the mass of magnesium carbonate that the student uses in the reaction.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0, Mg = 24.3, O = 16.0
answer_points: 0.1 mol of MgCO₃ reacts with 0.2 mol of HCl (the 1 : 2 mole ratio) (1)
Mass of MgCO₃ that reacted = 0.1 × 84.3 = 8.43 g (1)
worked_example.tip: The correct answer, 9.25 g, scores all four marks.
